rationales.LC: The lab says the traversal path is delivered by a prompt injection (S1) or a confused request, i.e. attacker-controlled language from ingested content or the request reaches the read_file tool-invocation path unmediated.
rationales.CP: This scenario only re-retrieves file content into the session; no evidence shows attacker-controlled context persisting into durable agent memory on this path, so no carryover is demonstrated.
rationales.AP: The effect relays from the model to the read_file tool within one agent under one principal and policy domain; no second agent, tenant, or trust boundary is crossed.
rationales.RH: No evaluator, verifier, grader, or reward channel is documented on this path, and no isolation test exists, so the evidence cannot decide whether a proxy is reachable.
rationales.ES: The tool surface is unconstrained in the baseline: all twelve tools are offered with unvalidated arguments, and remote MCP tool schemas are trusted unpinned.

score.automatable_rationale: The PoC is an automated test that calls Tools.call directly with the traversal payload; no human interaction or model judgment is needed to trigger the arbitrary file read.
score.technical_impact_rationale: The impact is arbitrary file disclosure readable by the agent process into model context; there is no evidence of integrity or availability loss on the agent system itself beyond the read.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: In the default CLI run a real Anthropic model decides which tools to call, with what arguments, and in what order across up to ten turns, and the harness executes those selections, including read_file paths.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models a tool-using office assistant whose model selects and sequences the twelve built-in tools; the scripted worst-case models in the tests stand in for the same loop.
